title: UK Recognises India's Carbon Credit Scheme, Easing Carbon Tax Burden on Exporters
excerpt: Britain has included India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme in its qualifying list under the UK CBAM, allowing Indian exporters to claim relief on carbon-intensive goods shipped to the UK.
body:
• The UK has formally recognised India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS) as a qualifying carbon pricing mechanism under its Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM)
  • Indian exporters of carbon-intensive goods like steel and cement can now claim carbon price relief in the UK, avoiding double taxation
  • The recognition follows the India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement signed in July 2026, with bilateral merchandise trade at $25.1 billion in 2025-26
  • The UK's CBAM takes effect in January 2027; India's early recognition gives its exporters a head start over competitors

A Win for Indian Exporters

The United Kingdom has formally recognised India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme as a qualifying carbon pricing mechanism under Britain's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism, a move that will directly reduce the carbon tax burden on Indian goods entering the UK market.

The recognition was communicated by the UK's HM Treasury to India's Bureau of Energy Efficiency under the Ministry of Power, a government official said on Monday. India's CCTS has been included in the UK's published indicative list of overseas carbon pricing schemes that meet qualifying criteria under the CBAM regulations of 2026.

"This will reduce the effective CBAM liability on Indian goods, directly benefiting Indian exporters to the UK," the official said.

How the Relief Works

Under the UK's CBAM, which takes effect in January 2027, importers of carbon-intensive products such as iron, steel and cement must pay a charge based on the carbon emissions linked to those goods. The mechanism is designed to prevent "carbon leakage" — where production shifts to countries with weaker climate rules.

With India's CCTS now recognised, UK importers of eligible Indian goods can claim carbon price relief corresponding to the carbon price already paid under India's domestic scheme. The relief avoids double taxation — once in India and again at the UK border.

However, the relief is not automatic. UK importers must satisfy evidence and verification requirements prescribed under UK law, and the quantum of relief depends on the effective carbon price applicable to the specific goods.

Building on Trade Momentum

The recognition follows sustained technical-level engagement between London and New Delhi and comes on the heels of the India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), which the two countries signed on July 15, 2026. Bilateral merchandise trade stood at $25.1 billion in 2025-26, while services trade reached $35.4 billion in 2024.

"India communicated to UK officials that CBAM is a disguised trade barrier that penalizes developing countries for their stage of industrial growth."

— Indian government official, as reported by Livemint

India had been pressing for recognition of its domestic climate mitigation efforts as part of broader sustainability cooperation. The Commerce Ministry pursued the matter with the UK government for an extended period, according to officials.

What It Means for NRI Business Owners and the Diaspora

For Indian-origin business owners in the UK who import steel, aluminium or other carbon-intensive products from India, the recognition could mean lower compliance costs and more competitive pricing. India's total engineering exports reached an all-time high of $116.67 billion in 2024-25, with $4.28 billion going to the UK alone.

The recognition also sets a precedent. India is simultaneously pursuing similar arrangements with the European Union, which began its own CBAM transitional phase in 2023. A successful UK template could strengthen India's hand in EU negotiations.

What's Next

Cooperation on carbon market design will continue through the UK-India Energy Memorandum of Understanding and the Partnership for Market Implementation. Both governments have committed to ongoing dialogue on carbon pricing, including how India's CCTS interacts with evolving UK CBAM rules.

With the UK CBAM set to go live in January 2027, Indian exporters now have several months to prepare documentation and ensure their carbon price payments qualify for relief under the new framework.
